title: Rotherhithe & Surrey Docks
intro: A riverside village of old warehouses, docks and churchyards, with the Thames Path on the doorstep and views to Tower Bridge and Canary Wharf.

items.name: Stave Hill and Russia Dock Woodland
items.blurb: Woodland and an ecology park on the filled-in Surrey Docks, with a small man-made hill that looks out over Canary Wharf and the City.
items.tip: Climb Stave Hill at sunset for the skyline.

items.name: Greenland Dock
items.blurb: The oldest of the Surrey Docks, now a wide sheet of water ringed by homes and a watersports centre, with the Thames Path close by.
items.tip: Walk round the dock and out to the river for a circular stroll.

items.name: St Mary's and the Mayflower
items.blurb: Rotherhithe's 18th-century parish church and, next door, the Mayflower pub near where the Mayflower set out in 1620; her captain, Christopher Jones, is buried here.
items.tip: The pub's small jetty terrace looks straight onto the river.

items.name: Southwark Park
items.blurb: A Victorian park opened in 1869, with a boating lake, a bandstand, a rose garden and an art gallery in the middle.
items.tip: The lake and bandstand are the prettiest corner.

items.name: Brunel Museum
items.blurb: The engine house of the Thames Tunnel, the first tunnel built under a navigable river, begun by Marc Brunel with his son Isambard and opened in 1843.
items.tip: Check the listings for talks and events in the old shaft.

items.name: King Edward III's manor house
items.blurb: The excavated foundations of a moated manor house built for Edward III in the 1350s, on the riverside by Cherry Garden Pier.
items.tip: Free and always open: it's a quick stop on the Thames Path.
